## Historical audit: S0194

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/service_incident_01/retired/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. Offsets below are character ranges within the specified JSONL line.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1, [0,9211) | The requested goal was to reconstruct an indoor RGB reference in Blender/SceneAct, with separate meshes, materials, camera and lighting. The prompt requested an image specification and complete program, followed by render-based comparison. This is the **intended task**, not evidence that reconstruction occurred. The image is referenced by path but its pixels are not included in the supplied observations. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 2, [0,2635) | One fresh CLI session was launched with the image, read-only sandbox and tools disabled. It failed with exit code 1; the record reports zero tool calls and no observable model-turn count. There is no visible program, geometry change, autonomous exploration, execution or render. |
| Student `model_error`, line 3, [0,552); `scene_error`, line 4, [0,1613) | The failure propagated through `runtime.ask` as a Codex student exit. The trace points to a stderr log but does not include its contents, so the underlying cause is unresolved. |

**Scene checks and validation:** The prompt calls for multiple objects, colors and materials, multipart meshes, viewpoint and lighting, but no generated scene or image is visible. Therefore object count, textures, part connections, object pose, camera framing, illumination and render quality cannot be independently checked. No formal success or partial correctness is demonstrated; this is a **technical interruption**, not an established algorithmic failure or an empty patch. No teacher input, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or student adoption is recorded.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable operational lesson is to distinguish a failed model invocation from a failed reconstruction algorithm and inspect the actual error evidence before diagnosing it. Task-specific geometric or visual lessons cannot be established from this trace. Whether the reference was successfully processed internally, what caused the exit, and what any unobserved model output might have contained remain unknown.
